proof_summary: Assuming the claimed recurrence, the shifted terms \(b_n=a_n+1\) follow the Fibonacci matrix evolution; a modular exponentiation modulo \(195318521017\) at offset \(249580073233\) shows that two consecutive \(a_n\)'s would both be divisible by this modulus. Their gcd \(g>1\), while for their sum \(s\) one has \(s/g>1\), so equating the defining next term \(g+s/g\) with the claimed \(1+s\) gives \((g-1)(s/g-1)=0\), a contradiction.
